policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders no adverbial 'also' beside 'appointed seventy others', but a connective kai before heterous is routinely left unrendered in English, so the wording neither requires nor excludes it.
ASV text reads 'seventy others'; the number two appears only in the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities add and two', so the ASV's text omits duo after hebdomekonta.
ASV 'sent them two and two' renders the distributive equally well from ana duo or the doubled ana duo duo; the mapped note concerns the number seventy, not this phrase.
ASV opens 'And he said unto them' with a bare connective, and reserves 'therefore' for the oun of 'pray ye therefore' later in the same verse; oun here would have been rendered 'He said therefore'.
Pure word order: 'that he send forth laborers into his harvest' is the same English for ergatas ekbale and ekbale ergatas.
ASV 'behold, I send you forth' supplies the subject from the verb; an added emphatic ego leaves no separate mark in ASV English.
ASV's flat list 'no purse, no wallet, no shoes' repeats 'no' without a coordinating 'nor', which is compatible with either me or mede in an asyndetic English series.

'into whatsoever house ye shall enter' does not distinguish aorist eiselthete from present eiserchesthe, nor the word order; the only note here is an alternative_rendering about where 'first' attaches.
Word order only: 'if a son of peace be there' is identical for e ekei and ekei e.
'for the laborer is worthy of his hire' needs an English copula whether or not estin stands in the Greek, so the added verb is invisible.
'into whatsoever city ye shall enter' renders aorist eiselthete and present eiserchesthe alike.
ASV has 'that cleaveth to our feet': 'to our feet' renders eis tous podas, which the competing reading omits.
ASV ends 'the kingdom of God is come nigh' with no 'unto you'; the added eph' humas has no counterpart in the English.
'which were done in you' renders egenethesan and egenonto identically.
'sitting in sackcloth and ashes' carries no gender, so masculine kathemenoi and feminine kathemenai are indistinguishable in English.

ASV puts a question with a future passive verb, 'shalt thou be exalted unto heaven?', matching me ... hupsothese; the participial he ... hupsotheisa would have given a relative clause 'which art exalted unto heaven'.
A bare article before Hades leaves no trace in ASV's 'unto Hades'.
ASV 'thou shalt be brought down unto Hades' is passive and causative, rendering katabibasthese; katabese would have given the active 'thou shalt go down'.
ASV reads 'the seventy returned', and the chapter's textual note assigns the added 'and two' to the margin here as well ('and so in verse 17').
ASV 'I have given you authority' is perfect, rendering dedoka; the present didomi would have given 'I give'.
'nothing shall in any wise hurt you' renders ou me with either aorist subjunctive adikese or future adikesei.
ASV 'your names are written in heaven' is the resultative perfect engegraptai; the aorist egraphe would have given 'were written'.
ASV 'in the Holy Spirit' with the margin 'Or, by' renders a plain dative or en plus dative alike, and that note is an alternative_rendering about English wording.
ASV reads 'he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit' with no named subject 'Jesus', so it renders to hagio and not ho Iesous.
Word order only: 'for so it was well-pleasing in thy sight' is the same for eudokia egeneto and egeneto eudokia.
ASV begins the verse 'All things have been delivered unto me of my Father', with no 'And turning to the disciples he said'; the added clause is unrendered.
'to whomsoever the Son willeth' renders ho ean and ho an identically.

ASV 'made trial of him, saying' joins the participle asyndetically, but ASV also supplies and drops such connectives freely in this verse ('stood up and made trial'), so the kai is not settled either way.
A bare article in 'with all thy heart' leaves no mark in English.

ASV renders 'with all thy soul' for either en hole te psuche or ex holes tes psuches; the 'Greek from' gloss is a greek_gloss attached to the opening clause, whose preposition is ex in both readings of this unit's set.
'with all thy strength' is the same English for en hole te ischui and ex holes tes ischuos.
'with all thy mind' is the same English for en hole te dianoia and ex holes tes dianoias.
'desiring to justify himself' renders aorist dikaiosai and present dikaioun alike.
ASV opens 'Jesus made answer and said' with no connective at all, while it renders sentence-initial de elsewhere in the chapter as 'And'/'But' (10:2 'And he said', 10:37 'And he said').
'leaving him half dead' absorbs an added tunchanonta, which adds nothing translatable to hemithane.
ASV gives a single arrival, 'when he came to the place, and saw him', matching elthon kai idon; the added genomenos kata ton topon would leave two participles of coming for one English clause.
ASV 'when he saw him' supplies the natural object of idon without italics, so an explicit auton cannot be told from an implied one.
ASV reads 'And on the morrow he took out two shillings' with nothing for exelthon; no departure is rendered.

ASV 'he took out two shillings, and gave them to the host' has the sum before the verb of giving and resumes it by 'them', matching duo denaria edoken; edoken duo denaria would give 'gave two shillings to the host'.
ASV 'and said, Take care of him' has no 'unto him' for the added dative auto, which ASV renders explicitly where it stands (10:37 'And Jesus said unto him').
ASV 'Which of these three, thinkest thou, proved neighbor' has no 'then'/'therefore'; the chapter renders oun as 'therefore' where it stands (10:2 'pray ye therefore').
ASV 'And he said' renders the bare connective de; oun would have given 'He said therefore', as ASV renders oun in 10:2.
ASV opens 'Now as they went on their way, he entered into a certain village' with no 'And it came to pass', which is how ASV renders an introductory egeneto de.
ASV's 'Now as they went on their way, he entered' neither requires nor excludes kai autos eiselthen; the clause connective is absorbed by the English temporal construction.

ASV reads 'received him into her house': both the prepositional phrase and the possessive 'her' are rendered, which only auton eis ton oikon autes supplies; bare auton gives no house and eis ten oikian gives no 'her'.
ASV writes 'Mary' for both the Semitic Mariam and the Greek Maria.
'sat at the Lord's feet' renders parakathestheisa pros and parakathisasa para alike.
ASV reads 'at the Lord's feet', rendering kuriou; Iesou would have given 'at Jesus' feet'.
'my sister did leave me to serve alone' does not separate the itacistic kateleipen from katelipen in ASV English.
'bid her therefore that she help me' renders the imperative whether spelled eipe or eipon.
ASV reads 'But the Lord answered and said unto her', rendering kurios and not the named Iesous.
'troubled about many things' renders thorubaze and turbaze alike.
ASV's text reads 'but one thing is needful' (henos de estin chreia), and its mapped textual note puts 'but few things are needful, or one' in the margin as the other reading.
ASV 'for Mary hath chosen the good part' renders gar as 'for'; Maria de would have given 'but'/'and Mary'.
'shall not be taken away from her' renders both the bare genitive autes of separation and the explicit ap' autes.
